overview.description: Turnover Bridge is a 2-player trick game (more related to Whist than Bridge). 52-card deck, 26 each. Layout: 12 face-down in row + 12 face-up on top + 2 secret hole cards. Spades permanently trump. Play face-up cards or hole cards. When face-up played, turn over card beneath. Win 14+ of 26 tricks. Information warfare: visible cards vs hidden cards.

history.origins: Turnover Bridge is a two-player trick-taking game in the Whist and Honeymoon Bridge family. Honeymoon Bridge refers to any two-player adaptation of Contract Bridge; documented variants include Bridge with Semi-Exposed Dummies, where dummy hands have face-down cards with face-up cards on top and playing a face-up card turns the card beneath face up. Turnover Bridge uses this turnover mechanic with a 12+12+2 layout per player and fixed spades trump. Whist, the classic English trick-taking game, originated in England and was widely played in the 18th and 19th centuries; two-player variants became popular for couples and casual play.
timeline: 20th century: Two-player Bridge adaptations such as Honeymoon Bridge became popular for couples and casual play.

nullReasons.evolution: No documented evolutionary changes; game emerged as a stable tradition.

setup.dealing: 12 face-down in row + 12 face-up on top + 2 hidden hole cards.

rules.objective: Win 14 or more of the 26 tricks. Spades are permanent trump. Players use a 12+12+2 layout (12 face-down, 12 face-up on top, 2 hole cards); when a face-up card is played, the card beneath is turned over and becomes available.
rules.gameplay: Play any face-up card or hole card. Follow suit. Trump with spades if void. When face-up card played, turn over card beneath (now available). 2 hole cards kept secret. Highest trump or highest led suit wins trick.

strategy.advanced: Force opponent to reveal weak cards.

play_card.description: Play one card from your face-up row or from your two hole cards. Must follow suit if able; if void in led suit you may play a spade (trump) or discard. When you play a face-up row card, the card beneath it is turned face up and becomes playable.

engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card French deck comprising four suits: Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, and Spades. Each suit contains thirteen ranks: Ace, 2 through 10, Jack, Queen, and King, providing versatile options for various card games.
engine.suitDescription: Four traditional French suits: Hearts (Cœur), Diamonds (Carreau), Clubs (Trèfle), and Spades (Pique), each represented with standard French card iconography and distinct color coding for easy identification.
engine.rankDescription: Standard thirteen ranks per suit: Ace, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack, Queen, and King, where each rank has distinct value and meaning depending on the specific game rules and player strategies.
engine.dealPattern: Each player receives 26 cards arranged as 12 face-down in a row, 12 face-up on top of those, and 2 hole cards kept secret.
